jobs.instructions: Speak in clear Modern Standard Arabic as a warm, composed preschool teacher addressing a small class. Use a natural feminine speaking voice in a comfortable middle register, with a clear steady tone and small pitch variations. Sound attentive and gently encouraging, with understated expression. Use ordinary classroom speech with clear word beginnings and clean endings. Keep consonants clear and long vowels accurate and evenly timed, without stretching them for expression. Avoid breathiness, whispering, vocal fry and sing-song pitch glides. Read the supplied short Arabic phrase exactly once, as teaching speech. Preserve its written short and long vowels. Read the supplied lead-in as written, with a brief natural pause at the colon. Do not add any other words. No introduction, numbers, commentary, music or additional sounds. Pronunciation guidance only: /tim.saːħ/. The first consonant is ت /t/, immediately followed by short /i/ and /m/. Continue into /saːħ/ as one smoothly spoken Arabic word. Preserve the long /aː/ and final ح /ħ/. These directions are not spoken text. Say only the Arabic input; no explanation or letter names.
